description: A junior Computer Science major aiming for a career in Cybersecurity who is confident with command-line tools but struggles with manual memory management and low-level debugging in C.

nodes.title: OS Services and System Structures
nodes.description: Introduction to OS services, system calls, and the distinction between user and kernel mode.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This foundational core node introduces essential OS structures while respecting the student's some_prior_exposure to technical concepts.

nodes.title: Systems Programming Refresher in C
nodes.description: A refresher on C programming pointers, memory management, and basic systems-level syntax required for the upcoming projects.
nodes.personalizationRationale: For a student with some_prior_exposure, this single scaffolding node ensures readiness for systems programming without over-explaining basics they likely know.

nodes.description: Exploration of the process abstraction, including the Process Control Block (PCB) and the state transition diagram.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's some_prior_exposure, we move efficiently into the process lifecycle and context switching mechanics.
nodes.title: Process Concepts and Operations
Inter-Process Communication (IPC)
nodes.personalizationRationale: The student's some_prior_exposure allows for a deeper dive into the trade-offs between different IPC mechanisms in modern operating systems.
nodes.description: Mechanisms for process communication via shared memory and message passing (pipes, sockets).

nodes.title: Threading Models and Libraries
nodes.description: Distinguishing between threads and processes, exploring user vs. kernel threads and various threading models.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Building on some_prior_exposure, this node clarifies how threading libraries like Pthreads map to kernel-level resources.
With some_prior_exposure, the student will analytically evaluate scheduling overheads and policy goals.
nodes.description: Detailed analysis of scheduling criteria and algorithms including FCFS, SJF, Priority, and Round Robin.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms
Midterm Review (Ch. 1-5)
nodes.personalizationRationale: This checkpoint validates the knowledge of a student with some_prior_exposure across all foundational chapters.
nodes.description: Review of materials from OS Foundations through CPU Scheduling in preparation for the midterm.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Synchronization is a core requirement; the student's some_prior_exposure helps in understanding atomicity and hardware-supported instructions.
nodes.description: Understanding race conditions and implementing critical section solutions using mutex locks and semaphores.
nodes.title: Process Synchronization Primitives
Classic Synchronization Problems
nodes.description: Applying synchronization primitives to solve the Bounded-Buffer, Readers-Writers, and Dining Philosophers problems.
nodes.personalizationRationale: A student with some_prior_exposure benefits from mapping theoretical problems to practical multi-threaded coding scenarios.

nodes.title: Advanced Concurrency and Design
nodes.personalizationRationale: To challenge the student's some_prior_exposure tier, this node explores advanced concurrency trade-offs beyond the floor requirements.
nodes.description: Analysis of real-world concurrency bugs and high-performance synchronization patterns such as lock-free programming.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This core module covers the analytical modeling of resource allocation for students with some_prior_exposure.
nodes.description: Identification of deadlock conditions and the use of the Banker's Algorithm for avoidance and detection.
nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization and Avoidance

nodes.description: Logical versus physical addressing, contiguous allocation, and the implementation of paging and segmentation.
nodes.personalizationRationale: The student's some_prior_exposure provides the necessary context for understanding hardware-level address translation.
nodes.title: Main Memory and Paging Structure

nodes.personalizationRationale: This heavily project-relevant node leverages the student's some_prior_exposure to connect memory management with system performance.
nodes.description: Techniques for demand paging, page replacement algorithms (LRU, FIFO), and the impact of thrashing.
nodes.title: Virtual Memory and Page Replacement

nodes.description: Overview of I/O hardware, polling, interrupts, and the role of DMA in system performance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This required capstone node ensures the student with some_prior_exposure understands the interface between hardware and software.
nodes.title: I/O Systems and Performance
File System Implementation
nodes.personalizationRationale: The student's some_prior_exposure facilitates an understanding of how logical data structures map to physical storage.
nodes.description: Exploring file system structure, directory implementation, and allocation methods (indexed, linked, contiguous).
A comprehensive review session covering all course content from processes to file systems in preparation for the final exam.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This final assessment ensures the student with some_prior_exposure has mastered the cumulative knowledge required for the final exam.
nodes.title: Cumulative Final Review
